limitations.text: Every "E1 beats E0" sentence must say which is matched.
Measured on a val that is 41.7% near-duplicates

Every training-time `val_loss` / `val_bits_per_char` so far (E0, E1, E2, E3, E9, E10, K7) is measured on a val that is ~42% near-memorisable. **Absolute numbers are inflated.** Comparisons may be confounded if architectures memorise repeats differently (attention vs GDN recall).

Everything produced before Phase 2b on LM training is single-seed (E0-E3, E9; K7 sweep; K4 has 2 seeds). Treated as **exploratory** until replicated under section 2; Phase 2b (E10, E1, E11 at n = 3) is the first confirmatory comparison. The retro-audit is in `experiments/stats/proposed-claims.md`.

qual: [exploratory n=1], contaminated val (K9), pending clean-val re-score
reason: Audit b4 verified: E0 0.6063 vs E1 0.5846 is one seed each (runs E0-20261122-122059-s0, E1-20261122-124440-s0) on a val that K9 found 41.7% near-duplicated; policy §2/§3 require the [exploratory n=1] tag and no unqualified 'beats'. Status unchanged, qualifier corrected

limitations.text: SQ99 (v0.4.63): on out-of-corpus Python (330 local files, <20% overlap) E1 is +0.42% WORSE than E0 (CI +0.06..+0.78%) while 3.44% better on in-corpus clean val; the advantage may be corpus-specific. Exploratory n=1; out-of-corpus is confounded with format shift; E0 may be handicapped by init (SQ200).

Outside review 20:37 (computed, contaminated val, provisional): Phase 2b E10 (HF Llama at E0's exact shapes) seeds 0/1/2 = 0.5822/0.5854/0.5859 (mean 0.5845), i.e. ~3.7% below our E0's 0.6063, about the same size as C5's headline 3.6%; E1 seed 0 at its tuned LR = 0.5835, only ~0.2% below E10's mean. The E1-over-E0 headline may be largely an E0 baseline artifact (init; SQ200). The registered verdict (Q12) compares E1 with E10 on clean-val doc-level bits/char over 3 seeds.

qual: vs E10 at tuned LRs, clean80, 3 seeds, N1X
reason: Registered Phase 2b test (Q12) on the pre-registered PRIMARY metric (clean80 doc-level bits/char, Addendum A2): the registered C5 rule gives REFUTED: E10 0.2672 vs E1 0.2677 (E1 0.18% worse); paired n=3 df=2 diff +0.00048 bpc, 95% CI [-0.00056, +0.00151], p=0.18; neither registered condition holds (gap vs 2x pooled sd 0.0020; max(E1) 0.2687 > min(E10) 0.2662). The secondary val_loss verdict agrees (REFUTED, -0.14%). The earlier '3.6% better' was E1 vs the handicapped E0 baseline (E0 0.6063 fails E0-parity vs E10). Per A2 the primary-metric verdict is the status. Confirmatory Holm family (C5 + E11) still INCOMPLETE on the N1X (E11 not run there); the Phase 2b-5090 7-seed replication (R1) is the independent check.

reason: Independent single-SKU replication (Phase 2b-5090, RTX 5090, 7 seeds per arm, registered v0.4.74): E1 0.26795 vs E10 0.26772 clean80 bpc (E1 +0.08%), paired n=7 CI [-0.00087, +0.00132], p=0.64. Same sign as the N1X test; applying the registered C5 rule also gives REFUTED (E1 not below E10). Status unchanged (REFUTED). Across both SKUs (10 seeds per arm) E1 vs E10 is a tie within about +-0.4%.

SQ241: param-matched E1 (mlp 952, 10.62M non-emb) is +0.61% vs E10 (7-seed mean; P1 PASS, within +-1%) and +0.53% vs full E1 (P2 FAIL, bound 0.5%; paired CI [+0.05%, +1.21%]): part of E1's tie rests on its 0.5M extra MLP params

SQ200: E1's original 3.6% lead over E0 was an init artifact: E0 with flat init trails E10 by only +0.44%, and E1 itself is insensitive to init (E1-flat vs E10-hf +0.07%), so C5's tie is not an init handicap on E1.
